title: U2 Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton in Halftime Video for Packers‑Rams Thanksgiving Eve Show
body:
Fans of both football and music were treated to a surprise crossover on Thanksgiving Eve when U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U U

During the Wednesday night matchup between the Green Bay Packers and the Los Angeles Rams at Lambeau Field, the stadium’s halftime show featured the legendary Irish rock group U 2, who delivered a high‑energy set that culminated in a heartfelt tribute to the late Dolly Parton. The band performed a medley that blended their own anthems with a brief rendition of Parton’s iconic “Jolene,” accompanied by a montage of the country star’s career highlights projected on the Jumbotron. The unexpected homage sparked a wave of applause and social‑media buzz, with viewers praising the band’s willingness to step outside their usual repertoire and honor a music icon whose influence transcended genre.

U 2’s appearance marked the first time the group has performed at a National Football League halftime, a decision that reflects the league’s ongoing strategy to diversify entertainment offerings and attract broader demographics. While previous halftime acts have leaned heavily on pop and hip‑hop stars, the inclusion of a rock legend signals a shift toward more eclectic line‑ups that can appeal to both older fans and younger viewers who appreciate classic rock’s enduring relevance. For the band, the platform offered a rare opportunity to reach a massive live audience—estimated at over 70,000 in the stadium and tens of millions watching on television—while aligning themselves with a cultural moment that celebrates American music heritage.

The tribute to Dolly Parton resonated particularly strongly because the country legend passed away just weeks earlier, leaving a void in the music world that many felt still needed to be acknowledged. By integrating Parton’s signature song into their set, U 2 not only paid respect to her legacy but also underscored the interconnectedness of musical genres. Lead vocalist Bono’s spoken dedication, “She taught us how to write a story that sticks,” was met with a standing ovation, highlighting how the band’s message of gratitude transcended the usual halftime spectacle. Critics have noted that the gesture added emotional depth to an otherwise high‑octane performance, turning the halftime interval into a moment of collective remembrance.

Reactions on social media platforms were overwhelmingly positive, with hashtags like #U2Tribute and #DollyPartonLive trending within hours of the game’s conclusion. Fans lauded the band’s willingness to honor Parton, while some commentators debated whether the inclusion of a tribute to a deceased artist was appropriate for a sports entertainment setting. Nonetheless, the consensus leaned toward appreciation for the sincerity of the homage. Moreover, the performance sparked renewed interest in Parton’s catalog, with streaming services reporting a noticeable uptick in plays of “Jolene” and other classics in the days following the broadcast.

Industry analysts see this collaboration as a potential blueprint for future halftime productions. The NFL, which has faced criticism over repetitive musical selections, may view the success of U 2’s genre‑blending set as evidence that fans are receptive to more varied and culturally resonant acts. Additionally, the partnership could open doors for other veteran musicians to join the halftime roster, offering a platform that bridges generational gaps and celebrates a wider spectrum of American music. As the league prepares for the upcoming holiday season, the positive reception could influence the curation of future events, prompting organizers to prioritize artistic diversity and meaningful tributes over pure spectacle.
